title: Underpromote with check
text: Remove the rook with a queen sacrifice so the f-pawn can advance. Black threatens mate after a queen promotion, but promotion to a knight checks and forks the queen.
demonstration: Qc8+ Kh7 Qxe6 fxe6 f7 h3 f8=N+ Kg7 Nxg6 Kxg6
bookLines: Qc8+ Kh7 Qxe6 fxe6 f7 h3 f8=Q Qxg2#

title: Block the king’s path
text: The king can initially catch the b-pawn. Sacrificing the d-pawn blocks the diagonal it needs, letting the b-pawn escape the king’s square.
demonstration: d6 exd6 b5 Ke5 b6 Kd5 b7

title: A knight blocks the pursuit
text: White’s queen exchange seems to let the king catch the h-pawn. Black’s knight move instead blocks the king’s route. This example begins with White’s mistaken move; Black then exploits it.

title: Promotion threat and skewer
text: Sacrifice the b-pawn to force the c-pawn off its file. Advance the a-pawn to draw the rook onto a7, then check on g7 before winning the rook.
demonstration: b6 cxb6 a7 Rxa7 Rg7+ Ke6 Rxa7

title: Deflect the promotion defender
text: Black sacrifices the rook on e1 to draw White’s rook away. A queen check then deflects White’s queen from the promotion square, and the pawn promotes with mate.
